newsitem.title: UK: BT to fall subject to government tax - ITN.
newsitem.headline: BT to fall subject to government tax - ITN.

text.p: Independent Television News said on Wednesday that British Telecommunications Plc would fall subject to the new Labour government's windfall tax on utilities.
The television channel, quoting Whitehall sources, said British Airways would not be subject to the tax. It gave no further details.
BT has fiercely contested the introduction of the tax on the basis that it is not a monopoly and should therefore be excluded from the levy.

ITN quoted Whitehall sources as saying that the others to be hit by the tax include the 10 water and sewage companies and the 12 regional electricity companies, the power generators and British Gas. However, the ITN report said the list was not exhaustive and could include airports operator BAA Plc.
ITN said the levy was expected to raise between three and five billion pounds ($4.9 billion), and is aimed at getting 250,000 young people back to work.
Britain's finance ministry said the report was speculation and that the Chancellor would outline the terms of the tax in his July 2 Budget statement.
